judged_text: A new unconditional network call to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update is inserted immediately before jsforce.Connection creation, which runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, where previously the connection reused stored tokens and jsforce refreshed only on demand. Every operation that instantiates the service (event bookings, availability checks, cron availability scans) now pays a blocking Salesforce token round-trip and a DB write even when the stored access_token is still valid; a Salesforce outage or added latency directly slows booking flows that previously never hit Salesforce at construction time.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an unconditional `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` refresh-token request and then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (added block around lines ~72-108 in the diff). There is no check for whether the existing `credential.key.access_token` is still valid/expired, so every construction of `SalesforceCalendarService` will incur a network round-trip and a DB write, potentially adding latency and coupling booking/availability flows to Salesforce uptime. This is a concrete perf/architecture regression grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a functional correctness defect.
